angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 11,847,771 km at 37.68 pc = 4.2 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 95689: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 26.54 +/- 0.48 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 37.679 +/- 0.681 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 17.03 +/- 0.13 solar radii from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 95689: radius 17.03 +/- 0.13 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 6.419 +/- 0.041 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 11,847,771 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 3.44 +/- 0.11 solar masses from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 95689: mass 3.44 +/- 0.11 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5012 +/- 65 K from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 95689: effective temperature 5012 +/- 65 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 95689: effective temperature 5012 +/- 65 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/dubhe.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 2.512, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf UMa: spectral type G9III+A7.5 (2014yCat....1.2023S)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf UMa: main object type SB*, Spectroscopic Binary
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * alf UMa: projected rotation speed 6 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2025A&A...698A..93J)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
